A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LD-MoLE and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding methods, results, and proofs can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations on Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen3-1.7B, together with routing analyses and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds MMLU-Pro evaluations, an 8B-model comparison, and computational-cost results in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: The Sparsegen router, shared MLP predicting token-specific λ, LoRA architecture, and training losses remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 proposes generating λ through an augmented gating projection only as future work.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMLU-Pro, extending the existing NLP suite with multi-domain knowledge and reasoning questions offering ten answer choices. All eight original benchmarks remain; the added 8B model changes experimental configuration rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MoLA(8888), MoLA(2468), and ReMoLE as comparators. The added evaluations and FLOP comparison reuse these methods. Newly cited AdaMoE, Ada-K Routing, and LongCat-Flash are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds an 8B configuration with a stated three-epoch budget and a router-plus-LoRA FLOP metric excluding backbone computation. Existing configurations retain their settings. The new setup is inconsistently documented: Table 1 says Llama3.1-8B, the prose says Llama-3.2-8b, and Appendix D still gives ten epochs generically.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 extends the existing sparsity-coefficient analysis by examining computational cost across β values and against routing baselines. The fixed-versus-predicted λ, zero-activation, training-pattern, local-versus-shared MLP, and hidden-dimension analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 3's existing 25–75 quantile visualization of λ distributions is unchanged.

E6.justification: The evidence expands substantially through MMLU-Pro scores, the full 8B comparison, and computational-cost results. Table 1 reports an 8B average of 85.18 for LD-MoLE versus 84.47 for ReMoLE. Original task scores remain identical; LD-MoLE averages change from 86.10 to 82.05 and 85.10 to 81.63 because MMLU-Pro enters the averages. New Table 6 reports 106 to 83 MFLOPs as β increases from 0 to 1, versus 43/40 for the MoLA variants and 74 for ReMoLE.

T1.justification: The equations, propositions, lemma, and Appendix A–B derivations retain their mathematical content. Appendix B corrects an internal reference from Proposition 2 to Proposition 1 without changing the proof; Section 3.1 expands the explanation of TopK discontinuities.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution list and conclusion extend the empirical performance claim to an 8B model. The central claims about learnable dynamic routing, analytical sparsity control, and superior average accuracy remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly identifies the shared λ-predicting MLP as the main source of computational overhead relative to TopK and ReLU routing, and suggests an augmented gating projection as future mitigation. This adds a concrete efficiency qualification to the existing sparsity–accuracy discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, documents the three-epoch budget for the added 8B experiment, and specifies that FLOP accounting includes routing and LoRA experts but excludes the backbone. The existing hyperparameter table is retained as Table 7.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of AdaMoE's null experts and Ada-K Routing's sampling/RL approach, plus a LongCat-Flash citation. MMLU-Pro is also newly cited. These are focused additions to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds conference-header text, acknowledgements, localized explanations and experimental paragraphs, and corrects the Appendix B cross-reference. The original section sequence, method exposition, and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a MMLU-Pro column and an 8B-model block, and Appendix C.3 gains the FLOP table. The hyperparameter table is renumbered from 6 to 7. Existing figures are retained, with Figures 2–4 relocated through text reflow and conference headers added.

improvement.justification: MMLU-Pro and 8B results broaden empirical support, while the new FLOP analysis makes the sparsity–computation trade-off and additional routing overhead more transparent. The code link also improves access information. These are useful incremental gains, tempered by inconsistent 8B model naming and unreconciled three-versus-ten-epoch descriptions that limit reproducibility of the new comparison.
